```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# DATA 202 hack for displaying plotly within RStudio:
if 'r' in globals() and r['.Platform$GUI'] == "RStudio" and r['suppressMessages(requireNamespace("htmltools"))']:
  r[".GlobalEnv$to_html <- function(x) { print(htmltools::HTML(x)) }"] and None
  def show_plot(p): r.to_html(p._repr_html_())
else:
  def show_plot(p): return p
# End hack
```

::: {.callout-important}
Please shutdown your RStudio session when you're not using it.
:::

In the past several exercises, you've typically been given a lot of template code and very specific instructions. This time, we'll do some of the same tasks, but without the training wheels.

For example, you should make your own `qmd` file. You may use past exercises as inspiration, but avoid copy and paste.

```{python}
daily_rides = pd.read_csv("../../static/data/bikeshare/day_by_type.csv", parse_dates=["date"])
```


## Exercise 1

Replicate this plot, made using the ridership data from the previous exercise. Write one or two sentences about what it tells you.

```{python}
show_plot(
  px.scatter(
    daily_rides,
    x="date", y="rides", color="rider_type",
    facet_col="workingday",
    trendline="lowess",
    labels={"date": "Date", "rides": "Number of Rides", "rider_type": "Type of Rider"}
    )
    .update_traces(marker_size=3, marker_opacity=.5)
)
```

- [ ] Have you replicated the plot?
- [ ] Are all the labels correct?
- [ ] Have you set the marker size (attribute `marker_size`) to 3?
- [ ] Have you set the marker opacity (attribute `marker_opacity`) to 0.5?
- [ ] Have you written one or two sentences about what the plot tells you?

## Exercise 3

Now use the gapminder data; you may use the data from Plotly Express. The following code chunk also creates some filtered data frames that are needed for the following exercises.

```{python}
#| echo: true
gapminder = px.data.gapminder()
just_usa = gapminder.query("country == 'United States'")

countries = [
  "China", "India", "United States",
  "Indonesia", "Brazil", "Pakistan",
  "Bangladesh", "Nigeria", "Japan"]

gapminder_9_countries = gapminder.query("country in @countries")
```

Make the following plot:

```{python}
show_plot(
  px.line(
    just_usa,
    x="year", y="lifeExp",
    labels={"year": "Year", "lifeExp": "Life Expectancy (years)"},
    title="Life Expectancy in the United States",
  )
  .update_traces(line_color='green')
)
```

- [ ] Are your axes labeled?
- [ ] Does the plot have a title?
- [ ] Is the line `green`? (The trace attribute is called `line_color`.)
